title: Active Object

validation.research: Six primary sources: Lavender and Schmidt’s original Active Object paper, the authors’ POSA Volume 2 catalog, official Python queue/concurrent.futures/threading documentation, and Akka actor-model documentation. Concurrent Object is preserved as an alias. The original paper’s historical Actor term is acknowledged while broader actor messaging/supervision semantics remain distinct. Proxy, method request, activation queue, scheduler, servant, future, optional guard scheduling, immutable argument/result boundaries, queue capacity, accepted FIFO order, cancellation states, callback self-waits, and graceful non-daemon lifecycle are explicit. A generic multi-worker executor is not assumed to serialize one mutable servant.

example_limits: Original Python 3.11+ real threaded custom executor for one stock owner. The proxy accepts integer item deltas, rejects Boolean/noninteger inputs, captures immutable deltas and Future references, and admits with put_nowait into a two-place FIFO activation queue. One non-daemon worker owns local quantity and performs every check/update. Zero change queries through the same queue. Negative stock fails before mutation and reaches its future; later work continues. Queued cancellation skips execution when the worker dequeues it, but does not remove its physical queue place early; running cancellation fails and a result-wait timeout is not cancellation. Admission and close share a lock, while servant state relies on worker confinement. Close marks admission closed, appends one stop marker after accepted requests without holding the control lock during a blocking queue put, drains and joins; worker self-join is rejected. task_done balances requests including cancellations and the stop marker. Repeated/concurrent close and 100 updates from four producers are verified with finite gate-based tests, without claiming fairness or caller start ordering. Futures are for observation/cancellation rather than manual client completion. A stuck worker/callback can make close wait indefinitely, and unexpected worker death has no restart/unresolved-request recovery. No guard scheduling, durable mailbox, actor-runtime supervision, distributed execution, external I/O, forced interruption, cross-object transaction, general rollback, or CPU-parallelism guarantee is inferred.
